summary: Jon Postel's revised list of standard host names, which tries to match the names used by the Network Information Center. He also gives a four-character alternate list, noting that programmers like short names made of simple characters. It replaced RFC 229.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 236 lists proposed names for ARPANET hosts and gives short alternatives for use by programs. It revises an earlier list and suggests consulting each host's technical liaison before assigning a name.

questions: who proposed standard host names arpanet
what were the standard host names in rfc 236
subtitle: A revised table of proposed standard host names and four-character alternatives.

tldr.problem: Earlier proposals differed on standard host-name length, and users also wanted short names suitable for limited host software.
tldr.mechanism: Jon Postel presents a revised list of standard names and alternate names of up to four characters using capital letters and digits.
tldr.outcome: RFC 236 obsoletes RFC 229. The list is a proposal for host names, not a protocol specification.

sections.title: Earlier Host-Name Proposals
sections.content:
RFC 226 suggested standard host names six characters long and included a partial list. RFC 229 proposed names eight characters long and provided a longer list.

RFC 236 presents Postel's list again with modifications. It suggests matching the Network Information Center's site names where possible and consulting a host's technical liaison before assigning its name.
sections.plainLanguage: Earlier notes proposed host names of different lengths. This note revises one list and recommends checking names with each host's liaison.

sections.title: Short Alternate Names
sections.content:
The author says programmers may prefer strings no longer than one computer word and limited to capital letters A-Z or digits 0-9. He therefore includes an alternate list limited to four characters and those alphanumeric characters.

For example, the standard name UCLA-NMC is paired with alternate NMC, and SRI-ARC is paired with NIC.
sections.plainLanguage: The alternate names are shorter and use only capital letters and digits. The table gives a standard name and a short alternative for listed sites.

sections.title: The Site Name Table
sections.content:
The table pairs site numbers with a standard name and an alternate name. It includes sites such as UCLA-NMC, SRI-ARC, UCSB, UTAH, BBN-NCC, and MIT-DMCG.

The listed entries include site 158, BBN-TIP, with alternate name BBNT.
sections.plainLanguage: The table connects a site number to a standard host name and an alternate name. It includes entries for universities, laboratories, and other listed sites.
